title_from_original: Different protocols in the same Service definition with type=LoadBalancer

initial_behavior.baseline: Kubernetes rejects Service definitions with different port protocols when their type is LoadBalancer. Cloud-provider implementations have differing capabilities; the document also describes existing provider-specific mixed-protocol annotations and shared-IP workarounds.
initial_behavior.requested: Lift the API's mixed-protocol limitation so a single LoadBalancer Service can describe different port protocols and reach the existing provider controller, with the goal of serving different L4 protocols through one IP where the provider supports it. Whether and how to retain option control is unresolved.

scope_rationale: The concrete change relaxes a validation limit on the existing Service/LoadBalancer capability and passes the newly accepted case to existing controllers (lines 98-117). The proposed control mechanisms are alternatives for this bounded change (lines 261-286).

mandatory_conditions.predicate: When the proposed mixed-protocol support is active, permit a Service of type LoadBalancer to declare ports with different protocols; do not reject the definition solely because its ports mix protocols. The original example includes UDP port 53 and TCP port 53 in one Service.

Pass accepted mixed-protocol Service definitions to the cloud-provider load-balancer controller; the controller logic and backing load-balancer capabilities determine the actual exposure of the application.
For a provider that can realize the requested protocol combination, support the user's goal of exposing an application through one cloud-provided load-balancer IP with different L4 protocols.

preferred_conditions.predicate: Consider an activation-control mechanism that lets unsupported or unwilling cloud-provider implementations avoid participating; the original does not settle the mechanism.
Make the user's acceptance of mixed-protocol load-balancer exposure explicit if an opt-in design is chosen, addressing the document's concern about unexpected provider charges.

unnecessary_conditions.predicate: Do not require both per-Service annotation opt-in and provider-side merging of separate Services; the source presents these as alternative control approaches.
Uniform realization of every protocol combination by every provider is not required; actual support and resource realization remain dependent on the provider controller and backing service.

initial_behavior.baseline: ComponentConfig files can share common parameters among component instances through one ConfigMap. Instance-specific values such as a host IP or hostname cannot be shared this way and have remained command-line parameters; existing deployments therefore combine a shared config file with instance-specific flags.
initial_behavior.requested: Add a separate versioned {Component}InstanceConfiguration Kind and --instance-config file interface for instance-specific parameters, while preserving shared configuration, legacy flag precedence, and the isolation of instance values from Dynamic Kubelet Config replacement.

scope_rationale: The proposal defines a separate top-level configuration Kind and consumption interface (lines 158-166 and 208-223), with concrete file delivery/use and refresh behavior (lines 289-356). Although it migrates existing parameter meanings, its new configuration API has a usable contract beyond a new flag alone.

mandatory_conditions.predicate: Introduce a separate top-level Kind for instance-specific parameters, using the naming convention {Component}InstanceConfiguration in the component's existing configuration API group.
Keep sharable parameters in separately shareable ComponentConfig files so concurrent component instances can continue using a single ConfigMap; deliver instance-specific files separately.

Use --instance-config as the canonical flag for the instance-specific file. Initially do not permit the instance-specific object in the --config YAML stream, or the sharable object in the instance-specific file.
Existing command-line flags for instance-specific parameters continue to function and take precedence over values read from the configuration file.
When Dynamic Kubelet Config consumes remote configuration, replace only values supplied through --config; the instance-specific parameters remain separate from that shared-config replacement.
An old kubelet cannot consume the new instance-configuration format. A new kubelet can consume the new format or continue using the old form until the stated deprecation period expires.
Restrict the instance-specific Kind to parameters that are genuinely instance-specific, rather than moving sharable parameters into it.

preferred_conditions.predicate: Permit deployment-specific generation of the instance file, such as a node startup script or an init container using the Downward API; these examples are alternative delivery approaches, not simultaneous requirements.
Keep component parameters on a consistent versioned configuration API surface as the migration proceeds.

unnecessary_conditions.predicate: Redesigning the existing parameter set or eliminating instance-specific parameters is not required.
Automatic detection of instance-specific values is not required to implement the separate-object approach.
Changes to the Dynamic Kubelet Config feature or remedies for its existing difficulties are outside this proposal's requirements.
Immediate removal of legacy command-line flags is not required; compatibility is retained and eventual removal follows the broader ComponentConfig deprecation strategy.

initial_behavior.baseline: Existing AppArmor support uses beta annotations on Pods and PodSecurityPolicies to choose profiles and define allowed/default profiles. Profiles must be available on the node and the runtime applies them. Pod annotation updates are accepted but only affect a container after restart, with no API indication of the effective value.
initial_behavior.requested: Promote the existing feature to GA, replace annotations with functionally equivalent dedicated fields, and deprecate the annotations. Bridge both representations in the API server for creation, updates, validation, policy enforcement, and version skew. New kubelets use immutable Pod fields and ignore annotation updates.

scope_rationale: The source explicitly upgrades existing annotations to equivalent fields and excludes functional enhancements (lines 94-97, 121-138, and 149-152). Its detailed contract concerns compatibility, validation, and representation transitions, including a bounded annotation-update change (lines 260-347).

mandatory_conditions.predicate: The dedicated AppArmor fields retain the beta API's profile-selection, allowed-profile, and default-profile functionality and the existing error propagation; the proposal does not change the default profile or introduce new confinement semantics beyond its expressly described transition behavior.

Provide optional AppArmor options at both pod and container security-context levels. The profile representation permits only one profile source and distinguishes Unconfined, runtime-defined, and node-local profiles; a node-local profile must be available on the node.
In PodSecurityPolicy, the default AppArmor profile must be permitted by allowedProfiles; if allowedProfiles is unspecified, the policy does not restrict AppArmor profiles.
An unspecified profile-set field excludes profiles of that type from the set. RuntimeProfiles may use '*' for all runtime profiles, and LocalhostProfiles may use a trailing '*' for prefix matching.
New kubelets use AppArmor values from the dedicated fields and ignore the annotations; API representation skew is resolved in the API server.
On Pod creation, if neither AppArmor annotations nor AppArmor fields are specified, take no AppArmor representation-conversion action.

On Pod creation with only AppArmor fields, add corresponding annotations for older kubelets. Retain this backfill through the specified skew transition and remove it in version N+4, where N introduces the upgraded AppArmor support.
On Pod creation with only AppArmor annotations, copy their values into the corresponding dedicated fields.
On Pod creation with both AppArmor annotations and dedicated fields, require matching values and enforce the requirement through API validation.
The dedicated AppArmor fields on an existing Pod are immutable.
Ignore subsequent AppArmor annotation updates in the new-kubelet behavior, without tightening the API validation that currently allows annotation updates.

For PodSecurityPolicy creation: do nothing when both representations are absent; backfill annotations from fields when only fields exist, removing this backfill in N+1; copy annotations into fields when only annotations exist; and validate equality when both exist.

For PodSecurityPolicy updates, apply creation rules when the old object had no AppArmor options; if only fields or only annotations change, copy the new value into both; if both change, require the new values to match through API validation.

During PodSecurityPolicy enforcement, read annotations when policy fields are unset to accommodate upgrade/skew; set only the field when defaulting and let API machinery backfill annotations; check both annotation and field values when enforcing allowed profiles because the effective value can depend on node version.
Do not resolve the two representations on PodTemplates themselves; perform field/annotation resolution when the template is instantiated.

preferred_conditions.predicate: Use explicit option/profile structures that can accommodate future profile sources or profile-setting behavior without requiring those future enhancements now.

unnecessary_conditions.predicate: Changing the default AppArmor profile from unconfined or adding new confinement semantics is not required.
Kubernetes-branded standard profiles, a Kubernetes AppArmor profile format, loading profiles from outside the node, and Windows support are outside the proposed enhancement requirements.
New profile sources and a new policy for failures to set a profile are future extension possibilities, not mandatory current behavior.
Promoting Seccomp to GA is not part of this proposal; it is assigned to a separate KEP.

title_from_original: Promote Taint Based Evictions to GA

initial_behavior.baseline: The already implemented feature evicts Pods according to node-condition taints, with tolerationSeconds controlling how long a Pod remains bound. The source states that the feature was introduced in alpha in Kubernetes 1.6 and promoted to beta in 1.13. This eviction mechanism is baseline behavior, not a design introduced by this proposal.
initial_behavior.requested: Promote the existing feature to GA by enabling it by default through feature-gate logic, while preserving its functionality. Check that test coverage is sufficient and update status documentation.

scope_rationale: The proposal explicitly excludes functionality changes and identifies default-enabling feature-gate logic as its concrete behavioral transition (lines 55-65 and 70-71). The eviction/toleration mechanism at lines 42-45 is pre-existing baseline.

mandatory_conditions.predicate: Change the Taint Based Evictions feature-gate logic so the feature is enabled by default.
Preserve the existing Taint Based Evictions functionality while making the default-on transition; introduce no functional change to the existing feature.

preferred_conditions.predicate: Establish that existing test coverage is sufficient for graduation, using the described node-lifecycle, integration, and end-to-end coverage.
Update documentation to reflect the feature's GA status.

unnecessary_conditions.predicate: A new taint-based eviction algorithm is not required; the original mechanism is already implemented and its functionality is to remain unchanged.
Changing node-condition taint interpretation or tolerationSeconds semantics is not required and would fall outside the no-functionality-change proposal.
